message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | Los Angeles offset | Berlin offset | Time difference (Berlin – Los Angeles) |
|--------|--------------------|---------------|---------------------------------------|
| Standard time (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | **+9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| Daylight‑saving time (summer) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | **+9 hours** (Berlin is still 9 h ahead) |

**Why the difference can briefly change**

- **US DST** starts on the second Sunday in March and ends on the first Sunday in November.  
- **European DST** starts on the last Sunday in March and ends on the last Sunday in October.

During the short overlap when the US has already switched to DST but Europe has not (or vice‑versa), the time difference temporarily becomes **8 hours**. After both regions have switched (or both have reverted), it returns to the usual 9‑hour gap.

So, for most of the year Berlin is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles, with a brief 8‑hour shift during the weeks when the DST transition dates differ.
message.reasoning: We need to answer: time difference between Los Angeles (Pacific Time) and Berlin (Central European Time). But time difference depends on daylight saving. Los Angeles is UTC-8 standard, UTC-7 DST. Berlin is UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 DST. So difference: standard: 9 hours (Berlin ahead). During DST: Los Angeles DST (UTC-7) Berlin DST (UTC+2) difference 9 hours. Wait: Actually both shift same offset? Los Angeles DST +1 hour, Berlin DST +1 hour. So difference remains 9 hours. But if one is in DST and other not? Usually they shift at same time? Actually US DST starts second Sunday in March; Europe DST starts last Sunday in March. So there is a 1-week period where difference is 8 hours. Similarly at end of September/October. So answer: 9 hours normally, but 8 hours during the week when DST changes differ. Provide explanation.
